evidence: Read cold in CONTEXT.txt: the section opens "Doing self-hypnosis on my own seems far more useful than the very little I managed to do with a professional hypnotist." and the draft follows it once, verbatim: "One reason might have been that I was sober when I did that, and didn't feel that susceptible to hypnosis. But I think a bigger reason is trust and precision." CHANGE: it is what the_change says (two Emulate sentences ending on his own "trust and precision", with "One reason might have been" restoring his hedge "Maybe part of that"). FLOW: it answers the sentence before it (a possible reason the hypnotist session did so little), and the next paragraph ("When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using ... is slightly off") unpacks trust and precision, so the last sentence sets that paragraph up and nothing dangles. PRONOUNS: "that" in "when I did that" can only mean the very little he did with the hypnotist (nearest antecedent, echoes "managed to do"; reading it as self-hypnosis would make "didn't feel that susceptible" a non-reason), so C02 is clear, only a hair less explicit than SOURCE's "at the session". MEANING vs SOURCE.txt: sober and not especially suggestible are kept as a hedged part-reason ("didn't feel that susceptible to hypnosis" = "didn't feel especially suggestible"); trust and precision is kept as the bigger reason, and "a bigger reason" keeps the ranking that "not even the main reason" gave. "I think" matches the "I suspect" his words already carried, and "is" for "was" matches the present-tense paragraphs around it ("seems far more useful", "When I do it on my own"). Nothing is added: no new fact about his life (C03 absent), no study, person or product (C04 absent). TELLS: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 and find none PRESENT. The nearest calls: T18/T12 (a concession, then "But I think a bigger reason") is not present because the second sentence ranks the first reason instead of flipping or negating it, and the shape is his own in the published guide ("Maybe part of that ... The larger issue was"); T20 (paragraph ends on "trust and precision") is not present because that is his phrase and the thesis the next paragraph develops, not a clever closer, and the paragraphs after it end on a longer sentence and a parenthetical, so there is no run of polished short endings; T29 is absent because without the last sentence the main reason would go unsaid, so it adds a consideration; T07 is absent because "might have been" and "I think" carry real uncertainty about causes, as "seems", "may" and "felt like" do elsewhere in the section; T16 is absent (no "not X, it's Y"; the draft in fact drops the source's "that's not even the main reason"); T15 is absent (plain synonyms, no rarer-word swaps); T01 is absent (the first person is the section's own account, not an added stake); T06 is absent ("trust and precision" is made concrete by the next paragraph). Cosmetic only: three "that"s in one sentence (complementizer, pronoun, intensifier) read as ordinary speech. LINTER: one finding, "D9 follows the source order", accepted: the order (smaller reason, bigger reason, then the next paragraph's detail) is forced by the sense and is his own order in the published guide, and each sentence makes a real thought-turn (a hedged concession, then a ranking judgment) rather than filling a slot, so T13 and T09 are clear.
